interpretation: Instruction: 'The two arms should coordinate to lift a pot. Arm 0 should grasp handle 0, and Arm 1 should grasp handle 1. Then both arms should lift the pot up at the same height.' Robot: capx_robosuite_two_panda_lift, two Panda arms (robot0 -> end effector hand0, the primary, base at the robot-root origin, left in the agentview image; robot1 -> hand1, facing it from the right). Parallel-jaw grippers: stroke 0.08 m, max width 0.079 m, closed_empty 0.985, held_below 0.95, closing axis x, approach axis z. Only one camera (agentview, scene, with depth); no wrist cameras. The pot is a red open-top box, about 14 cm on each side, rotated about 45 deg, centred near (0.538, -0.019) with its bottom on the table (table z about -0.109). It has two rectangular loop handles along the yaw 135.7 / -44.3 deg diagonal, each about 11 cm wide and reaching to u=0.17 m from the pot centre, with the outer bar at u=0.15-0.17 and z=0.011-0.031 (2 cm thick). The green handle is on Arm 0's side, centre of its outer bar (0.4245, 0.0937); the blue handle is on Arm 1's side, outer bar centre (0.6536, -0.1297). I read handle 0 as the green handle, the one on Arm 0's side, and handle 1 as the blue handle on Arm 1's side. Each arm takes the handle in front of it; the opposite assignment would make the arms cross. Perception ids did not match handles cleanly: obj1 was the pot body merged with the green handle, obj3 the blue handle, obj2 a fragment of the pot's inside bottom, and they were renumbered after motions. So I located the handles by colour-thresholding the fused point cloud rather than by id. Goal state: each arm holds its own handle, and the pot is lifted clear of the table (I aimed for about 20 cm, well past a 10 cm 'lifted' margin) with both grippers at the same height so the pot stays level. Ambiguity: the instruction does not define handle 0 and handle 1 or a lift height; the colour and side assignment above is my reading.
plan: 1) Read the embodiment and locate the handles from the point cloud. Fit the pot body (red OBB) and the handle axis (pot centre to green or blue handle centroid), then take each outer bar's centre at u=0.16 m along the axis, z=0.021. 2) Top-down grasp on each outer bar, with the fingers closing along the handle axis so the pads close across the 2 cm bar. Use the finger yaw nearest each wrist's current yaw: hand0 -44.3 deg and hand1 135.7 deg (the other yaws put joint 7 at its limit). 3) Move both arms at once to a pregrasp 10 cm above the grasp height. 4) Re-measure. 5) Descend straight down to TCP z=0.018. 6) Close both grippers. 7) Lift both TCPs by the same dz together, in two stages (4 cm check, then 16 cm more), requiring the preview_both schedule to be 'simultaneous'. 8) Hold 1 s, verify, finish. Changes along the way: the first pregrasp height (z=0.14) gave a joint-2 near-zero singularity warning on hand0, so I lowered it to z=0.12, which previewed with no issues. After the pregrasp move the green handle, previously hidden behind hand0, was fully visible, so I refined the axis (137.3 to 135.7 deg) and the bar centres (shifts of 6 mm or less, mostly along the bar) before descending. For the lift, every height over about 12 cm warned of joint 2 crossing 0. I checked that the joint motion stayed smooth (peak about 0.25 rad/s, joints 1 and 3 nearly constant, tracking error under 0.1 mm) and accepted it. I split the lift into a 4 cm check stage and a 16 cm stage.

steps.what: Read observe(): instruction, embodiment, budget; listed objects; showed agentview and annotated ids
steps.why: Look first: identify the arms, grippers, camera and the pot and handles
steps.result: Two Pandas (hand0 on robot0, hand1 on robot1), one camera, 5000 steps at dt 0.05. Perception gave obj1 (pot plus green handle merged), obj3 (blue handle), obj2 (pot-bottom fragment). Step 0.

steps.what: Colour-thresholded the fused cloud (green, blue, red); fit the pot OBB and a handle-aligned (u, v) frame; histogrammed handle points
steps.why: Perception merged the green handle into the pot; I needed the exact outer-bar positions and the bar height
steps.result: Pot 13.7 x 13.5 cm, yaw -44.6 deg, centre (0.538, -0.019). Handles reach u = 0.07 to 0.17 m; outer bar at u about 0.16; tops at z 0.031, blue side faces down to 0.010. Blue bar centred in v (v-mid 0.003). Grasp points barG (0.420, 0.089) and barB (0.655, -0.128), annotated on the image and checked visually.

steps.what: ik_batch for both yaws per arm; preview_both pregrasp at z 0.14, 0.12, 0.10; check_batch of a full approach; inspected the gripper collision spheres
steps.why: Pick wrist yaws with joint margin, avoid a singular pregrasp, and check the arms against the scene
steps.result: Chose hand0 yaw -42.7 deg (margin 0.5 rad) and hand1 yaw 137.3 deg (margin 0.67 rad). z=0.14 warned of hand0 joint 2 near 0; z=0.12 was clean. No arm-link contacts, only finger spheres against the handles at the grasp, plus a -2 mm sphere contact of hand1's palm with the pot rim. I judged that one a sphere-model artefact: the palm spheres' lowest point sits 5 mm above the rim, and the real hand is higher.

steps.what: execute_both to the pregrasp (TCP z 0.12 above each bar, grippers open), 2.8 s
steps.why: Position both grippers above their handles
steps.result: Both TCPs reached their targets to under 1 mm; grippers opened to 7.97 cm. The image showed each gripper above its handle's outer bar. Step 56.

steps.what: Re-measured both handles from a fresh cloud
steps.why: The green handle was now unoccluded
steps.result: Axis yaw refined to 135.7 deg; bar centres refined to (0.4245, 0.0937) and (0.6536, -0.1297), shifts of 6 mm or less.

steps.what: execute_both: descend straight to TCP z 0.018 at the refined poses (yaw -44.3 / 135.7), 2.3 s, after check_batch (no arm-link contacts)
steps.why: Put the open fingers either side of each outer bar
steps.result: Both TCPs exactly on target. The image showed the fingers straddling the green and blue outer bars, and the pot had not moved. Step 102.
hand0 measured 0.728 (gap 2.18 cm) and hand1 0.749 (gap 2.00 cm): below held_below 0.95, far from closed_empty 0.985 and from 0, and matching the 2 cm bar, so both held. Step 122.

steps.what: Previewed lifts of 12 to 20 cm and inspected the joint velocities
steps.why: Every lift over about 12 cm warned that joint 2 crosses 0
steps.result: Joint motion smooth: peak |dq/dt| about 0.25 rad/s, joints 1 and 3 nearly constant, pos_err under 0.1 mm, schedule simultaneous, no errors. Accepted.

steps.what: execute_both: lift both TCPs by +4 cm together (1.9 s), then re-measured the cloud
steps.why: Check that the pot rises level with both grips before going high
steps.result: TCPs at z 0.0577. Handle tops rose 0.031 to 0.070 (both), pot lowest points -0.109 to -0.070, so the pot rose 3.9 cm, level. Grips at 0.734/0.738. Step 160.

steps.what: execute_both: lift both TCPs by +16 cm more (4.3 s), same schedule check and check_batch
steps.why: Lift the pot well clear of the table at equal heights
steps.result: Both TCPs at z 0.2174. Grips both at 0.734. Step 246.

steps.what: Verified from the cloud, the agentview image, 3D views and low rendered side views; hold(1.0 s); re-verified
steps.why: Confirm the final state and that nothing slips
steps.result: After the hold: green handle top 0.2297, blue 0.2294 (level within 0.3 mm). Pot lowest points 0.089 vs table -0.109, so it is raised about 20 cm. Pot OBB centre (0.537, -0.019, 0.161), yaw -44.4 deg, unchanged in xy and yaw. TCPs 0.2174/0.2173, grips 0.734. The rendered low views show a clear gap under the pot. Step 266.

steps.why: Every part of the instruction held
steps.result: Episode finished at step 266 of 5000 (about 13 s of motion), wall time about 11 min.

key_images.caption: Start: red pot with green handle (Arm 0 side, left) and blue handle (Arm 1 side, right), both arms at home
Planned grasp points on the outer bars (barG on the green handle, hidden behind hand0; barB on the blue handle)
Both grippers open, 10 cm above their handles' outer bars
Fingers straddling both outer bars at grasp height, before closing
Both grippers closed on their bars (readings 0.728 / 0.749)
After the first 4 cm synchronized lift: pot rose 3.9 cm, level
After the full lift: pot held by both arms about 20 cm above the table
Rendered low side view: pot (with handles at its top) clearly above the table plane
Final state after a 1 s hold: pot still raised and level, both handles gripped

lessons: 1) On this two-Panda pot-lift scene, perception merges a handle into the pot body and renumbers ids after motions. Thresholding the fused cloud by colour (green, blue, red) and working in a handle-aligned (u, v) frame gave the bar positions to a few mm. 2) Top-down grasps on each handle's outer bar, with the fingers closing along the handle axis, worked first try at TCP z = bar centre - 3 mm. The closed readings (about 0.73, gap about 2.1 cm) confirmed each bar was held. 3) Choose each wrist's yaw (yaw or yaw+180) by IK limit margin: the wrong one sits on the joint-7 limit. 4) The harness warns about joint 2 crossing 0 when a Panda TCP rises close to its base. Inspecting the preview's joint velocities showed it harmless here. Lowering the pregrasp removed the warning when it was avoidable. 5) For a two-arm closed-chain lift, require preview_both's schedule to be 'simultaneous'. A short first lift stage plus a cloud check (handle tops rising equally) confirms both grips before going high. 6) Sphere-model contacts between the palm and the pot rim at grasp poses can be artefacts. Compare the sphere envelope's lowest point with the obstacle height before trusting them.
